title: Broad Lean Corpus Build and Rich Isomorphism Status v0

canonical_node.axiom: The broader Lean corpus contains a richer structural testing layer that goes beyond equation-shape analogy, and its full build passes locally without active proof escapes.
definitions: Rich isomorphism: a mapping that preserves roles, transitions, signature discipline, gate behavior, and passes adversarial wrong-swap checks.
Proof escape: active use of sorry, admit, axiom, or unsafe in source files (excluding expected #check_failure diagnostics).
Seed kernel: a clean compressed assumption spine with 4 front-loaded assumptions and 17 no-sorry starter theorems.
Broad corpus: a richer formal archive with reported 287 theorems, zero sorry, zero admit, including rich isomorphism and adversarial layers.
derivation: The full build command 'lake build' completed successfully with 17 jobs.
The proof-escape scan found no active sorry, admit, axiom, or unsafe in main source files.
Targeted builds for Theophysics_Core, Theophysics_Adversarial, and other modules passed.
The corpus docs list RichLawIso, richLaw4Iso, no_rich_iso_to_natural_coin, richRelabeledCoinIso, BridgeMatrix, MasterEquationInvariance, and wrong-swap rejection rows.
The safe claim is that the framework does not rely merely on equation-shape analogy; it includes richer structural testing.
The boundary states that Lean verifies the encoded structure but does not independently prove domain-faithfulness of human labels.
canonical_node.action: Maintain the broad corpus as a separate build layer from the seed kernel; continue to verify the rich isomorphism layer and ensure no active proof escapes; do not merge the broad corpus into the seed package until theorem inventory is normalized.
boundary: Does not claim that Lean independently proves domain-faithfulness of human labels.
Does not claim that the reported 287 theorems are all substantive; wrapper/trivial rows may exist.
Does not claim that the rich isomorphism layer is fully verified beyond the encoded model.
Does not claim that the build success implies correctness of the underlying physics/theology.
test: Run the proof-escape scan and confirm no active sorry/admit/axiom/unsafe in main source files.
Check that the rich isomorphism components (RichLawIso, richLaw4Iso, etc.) are present in the corpus.
Verify that the safe claim wording is used in public statements.
Ensure the seed kernel and broad corpus remain separate build layers.

dg1_dependencies: Theophysics_Core, Theophysics_Adversarial, Theophysics_Coherence, Theophysics_Fracture, Theophysics_Fall, Theophysics_ChiEvaluator, Theophysics_NegativeInventory modules
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a richer structural testing layer (signature discipline, role/transition preservation, gate tests, adversarial wrong-swap checks) beyond simple equation-shape isomorphism.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: The seed kernel's clean compressed assumption spine and 17 no-sorry starter theorems remain intact as a separate build layer.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If the rich isomorphism layer is removed, the framework reverts to a weaker equation-shape analogy, losing the adversarial wrong-swap checks and signature discipline.

classification.recommended_atom_action: record as verified build status with boundary; do not upgrade to domain-faithfulness proof

overstatement_risks: Claiming that Lean proves domain-faithfulness of human labels.
Claiming that the reported 287 theorems are all substantive without normalization.
Claiming that the rich isomorphism layer is fully verified beyond the encoded model.
Treating build success as evidence of correctness of the underlying physics/theology.
kill_conditions: If an active sorry/admit/axiom/unsafe is found in main source files.
If the full build fails on a clean checkout.
If the rich isomorphism components are not actually present in the corpus.
If the seed kernel and broad corpus are merged without normalization.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the rich isomorphism layer in Lean with explicit role/transition preservation and adversarial wrong-swap checks, and prove that intended mappings pass while selected false mappings fail.

plain_summary: This document reports that a broader Lean corpus builds successfully and contains a richer structural testing layer for isomorphisms, including signature discipline and adversarial checks. It explicitly warns against overclaiming that Lean proves domain-faithfulness. The status is coherent and admissible, but the proof label is limited to runtime support, not formal proof of the underlying claims.
